Phase 68 implemented at e83da41 (3 commits: bf2e995 server, 89bd1dd front end, e83da41 what the live look found + docs). gate: see entry @ e83da41.

What / where
- tagteam/cockpit_api.py: status_facts(root) — the headline's inputs from reads that never open the DB (state file, config, in-flight + slot_owner_gone, pause marker, watcher_status, beat_view/last_event, new watcher.last_dispatch, beat.text); inflight_liveness() — starting | no-child | running | finishing | unknown | lost, 'lost' only on a definitively gone OWNER (or a legacy marker's confirmed-dead child); turn_delivered(); headline(facts, launch) — the approved first-match table; now_payload() now takes these facts from status_facts() and adds 'headline' (its one DB-derived input, the pending launch, is passed in). Existing now keys unchanged; inflight gains 'liveness'.
- tagteam/watchlog.py: watch status prints 'now: <headline> · <age>' first and is built from status_facts() only; read(..., include_info=False) drops info BEFORE taking the newest n and folds runs of the same (kind, msg, seq) into repeat/last_ts.
- tagteam/server.py: /api/watcher/events takes chatter=0|1 and FIXES A 3.14.5 BUG OF MINE: it indexed _qs()'s already-scalar value, so n=200 meant 2 and n=37 meant 3 (Phase 67's test used n=5).
- tagteam/data/web/cockpit.{html,js,css}: chip-owed / chip-inflight / chip-paused / chip-watcher removed; a full-width turn bar (<button aria-expanded aria-controls>) presenting n.headline with one locally ticking age; the watcher drawer (facts, Start/Stop moved here, why the page cannot run turns — START.headless.errors, also in the notify-mode confirm body — or 'agents are in their terminals', story history with 'show everything', follow-only-at-bottom + 'new events' cue, Esc, remembered in localStorage). New JS is one banner-delimited slice, createElement/textContent only.

Approval notes: turn_delivered() accepts only a terminal watcher's 'sent' with a non-null matching seq (notify and headless 'sent' never count; None never matches None); a pause after delivery reads '… has its turn; further hand-offs are held'; liveness 'unknown' reads as plain working, never 'finishing'.

Guards changed ON PURPOSE (tests/test_cockpit_activity.py), none deleted to get green: (1) required-id list: chip-owed, chip-inflight, chip-watcher out; turn-bar, turn-text, turn-age, watcher-drawer, wd-facts, wd-rows, wd-all, wd-new, btn-watcher, chip-cycle in; the four pill ids are now asserted ABSENT from html and js; bar must be a button with aria-expanded/aria-controls, in its own row, before the drawer, before Needs-you. (2) UX-words guard: 'is working' / 'waiting on' / 'watcher: on|off' no longer live in the JS — it now generates the real sentences from capi.headline over a product of facts and asserts the plain words are there and engine words (in flight, dispatch, slot, marker, seq, pid…) are not. (3) the fitLanes slice end-marker moved from the deleted renderOwedChip to the watcher-button handler. Also tests/test_watchlog.py: watch status expectations gain the first line; beat gains 'text'.

Tests: test_cockpit_api — liveness over markers written by the real slot writers (live gate owner + pid None, cycle and panel before spawn → running → dead child under live owner, dead owner, legacy, unreadable identity, unknown), the full headline table, priorities, the enumerated owed-turn product (3,600 combinations: never idle, agent always named, age always set), text never carries an age, status_facts with db.connect patched to fail; test_watchlog — watch status on a DB-less project with and without TAGTEAM_READ_ONLY leaves the tree byte-identical, story-mode filtering/folding, endpoint n=37/200 and chatter=0; test_cockpit_activity — six node-run tests of the new slice. Focused run of the eight front-end/API files: 405 passed.

Seen, not assumed (criterion 7; table + what each shot shows in the phase doc; screenshots under git-ignored .playwright-mcp/): this repo under its iTerm2 watcher with the terminals note; and in a scratch project: watcher-off, the watcher started from the drawer, 'codex is reviewing' live in the reviewer's colour, the automatic hand-off to the lead, approved with history, and a REAL stalled state (scratch watcher SIGSTOP-ped, new turn owed → red 'Stalled…', same sentence from watch status). The live look is what found five defects the green unit tests had not (cut-off sentence, the n bug, chatter burying the story, 48 identical turn lines per pre-check, 'working on the plan' while implementing) — all fixed and pinned by tests.

Deviation: while open, the drawer re-reads /api/now + events every 5 s (plan: the page's 30 s tick) because 'last look: 7s ago' must not sit frozen. Plan said chatter is hidden client-side; it is filtered server-side because the window is counted there.

NOT verified / not seen: 'waiting' under a terminal watcher with a turn owed (this repo was 'done' while I looked — it is on screen now, while you hold this submission), needs-you, turn-lost, paused, launching (table tests only); the start-impl verb fix was made after its screenshot and is verified by test only. Left for Phase 68b and recorded in docs/cockpit-issues.md: Needs-you stays calm while the bar says Stalled; the reviewer lane still says 'the watcher will start it'.

GATE: PASS | scope 12 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2270 passed, 5 skipped, 7m39s)
checked: HEAD e83da41

Reviewed e83da41 against the approved plan, including headline/status_facts, liveness and delivery semantics, frontend integration, guard changes, and the approved-with-history screenshot. Two reproduced history defects need correction:

1. tagteam/watchlog.py:263-268 chooses whether to read .1 using the pre-collapse record count. With n=200, 201 identical tagged events in the live file, and an older distinct sent event retained in .1, story mode returns just one folded row and never reads the older event. Reproduced with _records supplying these two generations: read(..., 200, include_info=False) returned only {kind: turn, repeat: 201}. Determine the needed history after folding (including runs spanning the boundary), or combine the two bounded generations before filtering/folding/taking n. Add coverage for a live run larger than n, a retained match in .1, and a run crossing the rotation boundary. The byte bound already makes the two-generation scan finite.

2. cockpit.js:311-330 detects new events by list length and preserves only pixel scrollTop. The API returns a rolling 200-row window: at capacity every new event leaves the length unchanged, so the cue never appears, and keeping the same pixel offset shifts the reader to a different event when the oldest row drops out. A folded row's repeat/last_ts can also change with no length change. Reproduced through the existing _run_p68 Node harness: render 200 events, scroll back, replace event 0 with new event 200; newEventCueHidden remains True. Detect new/updated history using event identity/content, preserve the visible event anchor and offset while it remains retained, and keep the unread cue until the reader follows/clicks it (currently even an unchanged next refresh clears it). Add capped-window, folded-update, repeated-identical-refresh, and anchor-preservation tests. The existing test that expects the cue to vanish on the next unchanged refresh should be revised deliberately.

The main headline and DB-free CLI approach address the plan findings and approval notes. Accepted scope adjustments: the multi-digit n parsing fix is correct for _qs's scalar values; server-side filtering before counting is needed to retain useful history; folding repeated story rows is sensible with the correction above. Five-second refresh while open is a reasonable scoped change. Existing keys and the no-UI-work-in-lanes boundary are preserved.

Verification: reviewer tests/test_cockpit_api.py + tests/test_cockpit_activity.py + tests/test_watchlog.py: 204 passed. git diff --check a7dae2b..HEAD clean. Gate PASS @ e83da41: 2270 passed, 5 skipped, accepted without rerunning the suite. Reviewer inspected .playwright-mcp/p68-6-approved-with-history.png; the header/drawer hierarchy is clear. Lead's disclosed unobserved states and the post-screenshot verb change remain accurately limited to automated coverage; retain those distinctions in closeout. No interjections present.
